items.title: Finite solenoidal Galerkin coefficient dynamics
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness conditional on the current Fourier supplier Step 1 record.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice: for every sequence $(X_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of nonempty sets there is a function $f$ on $\mathbb N$ such that $f(n)\in X_n$. For $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, let $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ carry the probability measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^d$ define $e_k:Q_d\to\mathbb C$ by $e_k([x])=e^{ik\cdot x}$; this is independent of the representative since $e^{2\pi i k\cdot n}=1$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^d$. For an integer $N\ge1$ and a Borel-measurable map $q:Q_d\to\mathbb R^N$ with $\int_{Q_d}|q(x)|\,d\mu(x)<\infty$ in the Euclidean norm, considered up to equality $\mu$-almost everywhere, define its componentwise Fourier coefficients by $\widehat q(k)=\int_{Q_d}q(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$; this integral is finite componentwise because $|e_k(x)|=1$. The supplied space $H^0(Q_d;\mathbb R^N)$ is the completion of finite real trigonometric polynomials in the norm $\|q\|_{H^0}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}|\widehat q(k)|^2$, identified with its unique $L^2$ representative; real classes satisfy $\widehat q(-k)=\overline{\widehat q(k)}$. For vector fields with these representatives, set $\langle v,w\rangle_2=\int_{Q_d}v\cdot w\,d\mu$. For an integer $r\ge1$, an admissible finite solenoidal family consists of classes $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in H^0(Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$ whose representatives are smooth $2\pi$-periodic fields satisfying $\operatorname{div}v_i=\sum_{m=1}^d\partial_{x_m}v_i^m=0$ and $\langle v_i,v_j\rangle_2=\delta_{ij}$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise. Given such a family, a parameter $\nu\ge0$, and a coefficient vector $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb R^r$, put $u_a=\sum_{i=1}^r a_i v_i$ and define

$$A_{ij}=\int_{Q_d}\sum_{\ell,m=1}^d(\partial_{x_m}v_j^\ell)(\partial_{x_m}v_i^\ell)\,d\mu,\qquad c_{ijk}=\int_{Q_d}\sum_{\ell,m=1}^d v_j^m(\partial_{x_m}v_k^\ell)v_i^\ell\,d\mu.$$

The unforced finite solenoidal Galerkin coefficient dynamics is the initial-value system for $a:[0,T)\to\mathbb R^r$,

$$a_i'(t)+\sum_{j,k=1}^r c_{ijk}a_j(t)a_k(t)+\nu\sum_{j=1}^r A_{ij}a_j(t)=0,\qquad a_i(0)=a_i^0,\quad i=1,\ldots,r,$$

where $T\in(0,\infty]$ is the right endpoint of the interval on which a solution is defined and $a^0\in\mathbb R^r$ is the initial coefficient vector. A solution on $[0,T)$ is continuous on $[0,T)$ and continuously differentiable on $(0,T)$, has a right derivative at $0$, and its derivative extends continuously to $0$ with that value; the ODE holds for $0<t<T$ and at $t=0$ using this right derivative. When $T<\infty$, no value or derivative at $T$ is required because $T$ is excluded; when $T=\infty$, no endpoint condition is imposed at infinity. The displayed integrals are finite because their integrands are smooth on the compact torus. This is a finite-dimensional polynomial ODE; this definition asserts no convergence to a solution of the infinite-dimensional PDE.

references.title: Emil Wiedemann, Lecture Notes: Navier-Stokes Equations, edited by Jack Skipper, Universität Ulm, Winter 2018/19
Lenya Ryzhik, Lecture Notes for Math 256B, Version 2019, Stanford University

items.title: Skew reduced convection and global finite dynamics
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness conditional on the current Fourier supplier Step 1 record.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, meaning every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function. Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $r\in\mathbb N$ with $r\ge1$, and $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ with probability measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-d}dx$. In the supplied Fourier-Sobolev convention, $H^0(Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$ is the completion of finite real trigonometric polynomials in the norm $\|q\|_{H^0}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}|\widehat q(k)|^2$, with unique $L^2$ representatives and conjugate-symmetric coefficients for real classes. Let $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in H^0(Q_d;\mathbb R^d)$ have smooth $2\pi$-periodic representatives satisfying $\operatorname{div}v_i=0$ and $\int_{Q_d}v_i\cdot v_j\,d\mu=\delta_{ij}$. Fix $\nu\ge0$ and $a^0\in\mathbb R^r$, set $u_a=\sum_i a_i v_i$, and define

$$A_{ij}=\int_{Q_d}\nabla v_j:\nabla v_i\,d\mu,\qquad c_{ijk}=\int_{Q_d}((v_j\cdot\nabla)v_k)\cdot v_i\,d\mu,$$

where $\nabla v_j:\nabla v_i=\sum_{\ell,m=1}^d(\partial_{x_m}v_j^\ell)(\partial_{x_m}v_i^\ell)$ and $((v_j\cdot\nabla)v_k)^\ell=\sum_{m=1}^d v_j^m\partial_{x_m}v_k^\ell$. Consider the coefficient initial-value system

$$a_i'(t)+\sum_{j,k=1}^r c_{ijk}a_j(t)a_k(t)+\nu\sum_{j=1}^r A_{ij}a_j(t)=0,\qquad a_i(0)=a_i^0,\quad i=1,\ldots,r.$$

There is exactly one solution $a\in C^1([0,\infty),\mathbb R^r)$ of this system. For every $t\ge0$, it satisfies

$$\frac12\frac{d}{dt}|a(t)|^2+\nu\int_{Q_d}|\nabla u_{a(t)}|^2\,d\mu=0,$$

$$|a(t)|^2+2\nu\int_0^t\int_{Q_d}|\nabla u_{a(s)}|^2\,d\mu\,ds=|a^0|^2.$$

This is a global result for the specified finite coefficient ODE only; it asserts no convergence to, existence of, or uniqueness for a solution of the infinite-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations. The Countable Choice assumption is inherited from the periodic Fourier-Sobolev framework; the finite-dimensional proof makes no further choice.

references.title: Emil Wiedemann, Lecture Notes: Navier-Stokes Equations, edited by Jack Skipper, Universität Ulm, Winter 2018/19

items.title: One shear mode reduced evolution
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness conditional on the current Fourier supplier Step 1 record.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, meaning every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function. On $Q_2=\mathbb R^2/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^2$ with normalized measure $d\mu=(2\pi)^{-2}dx_1dx_2$, take the single vector field $v_1(x_1,x_2)=\sqrt2\sin(x_2)e_1$, where $e_1=(1,0)$. This finite real trigonometric polynomial belongs to $H^0(Q_2;\mathbb R^2)$ and has its displayed smooth periodic representative. For every $
u\ge0$ and $a_0\in\mathbb R$, the one-mode reduced velocity $u(t,x)=a(t)v_1(x)$ has coefficient equation $a'(t)+
u a(t)=0$ and unique forward solution $a(t)=a_0e^{-
u t}$ for $t\ge0$. Its reduced energy $E(t)= rac12 a(t)^2$ satisfies $E'(t)=-
u\int_{Q_2}|
abla u(t,x)|^2\,d\mu$. This is an exact finite-mode calculation and asserts no convergence or approximation error for the full partial differential equation.
